Correction and verification update — October 17, 2026. Please read this historical version together with the dated correction notice and verification limits. Corrected software, complete lower-bound witnesses, and a corrected research-draft manuscript are archived at 10.5281/zenodo.23433640. The files and DOI of this historical paper version are unchanged.

Original description:

We define coprime Ramsey numbers R_cop(k) on the coprime graph G(n) and determine exact values R_cop(3)=11 and R_cop(4)=59 via SAT solving. We also compute R_cop(3;3)=53 for 3-color Ramsey, 25+ variant values, and prove R_gcd(3;d)=11d. All known coprime clique Ramsey values are prime. Adversarially verified.

records.description_before: Version 2 (June 10, 2026): strengthened edition. R_cop(4) = 59 is now a complete theorem: an elementary clique bound (the set {1} together with the primes up to n is a clique of size 1+pi(n), giving R_cop(k) <= p_{R(k,k)-1}) combines with the SAT lower bound, removing v1's caveat. Corrections: the restriction argument for R_cop(k) >= R(k,k) is stated correctly; the classical comparison values R(2,3)=3, R(2,4)=4, and gr_3(K_3)=11 are fixed (with correct values every asymmetric entry matches the prime-index identity of Du, Xi, Deng, and Ma, arXiv:2605.26815, who cite these computations); the independence-number proof is repaired for odd n. New observation: the Gallai value GR_cop(3;3) = 29 = p_10 equals p_{gr_3(K_3)-1}, suggesting the prime-index identity extends to the Gallai setting.
